newRun.title: New inventory run
newRun.hint: Pick a paging scheme and parameters. The run uses the currently initialized scene.

wizard.previewHint: Check these choices, then start the run.

newRun.name: Name (optional)
newRun.pFixedHint: Fixed frame size only. The reader writes this p* into every paging message, and a device that hears it joins with this probability. 1 means every device that hears the page joins. Value from 0 to 1.
newRun.adaptiveKHint: Round 1 uses the Initial $K$. Later rounds set $K \approx 2\hat{N}$ from the Schoute / empty-slot backlog estimate.
newRun.useGroupingHint: Periodic paging only. Devices are split into $N_g$ groups; each paging round invites one group in turn. A device joins the group of the first paging it hears (first-catch) and stays aligned to that group's paging times. Off: every paging round invites all devices.
newRun.useCaptureHint: When several devices pick the same Msg1 slot, the reader still decodes the strongest one if it is at least 6 dB above the next strongest. Off: every slot with two or more devices is a collision. For periodic paging the Msg2/Msg3 allocation is $0.5\,K$ with capture and $0.37\,K$ without.
newRun.useEbiHint: EBI is the early indicator (EI) of the aperiodic paper: after Msg1 the reader sends a one-bit flag per slot saying whether a response was detected, so devices know where their Msg2 is. On: each round spends that extra EI air time, and the reader's energy detector is modelled with false alarms and missed detections. Off: no EI time and ideal slot detection.
newRun.includeD2rHint: D2R is the device-to-reader uplink. On: a reader covers a device only if both legs close, so the range is $\min(R2D, D2R)$, as in the paper. Off: only the reader-to-device leg (power-up and paging) counts, which overstates coverage.
newRun.singleReplyHint: After a device joins one paging round, it ignores other readers until that round ends. The lock clears on success, collision, a missed detection, or depletion. Off: a device in an overlap can join two readers at once.
newRun.stationCwHint: The paper's multi-source case, on by default. Stations and readers both transmit a continuous wave, and a device harvests the sum. Stations do not page. Off: only readers charge, the paper's single-source case.
newRun.disableReadersHint: Checked readers are skipped for this run (handy for single-reader baselines).
newRun.allReadersDisabledWarning: All readers disabled — no device will be identified.
newRun.endHint: The run ends when every reachable device is identified, when nothing new is identified for the time above, or when you pause / stop it. Devices outside every reader’s coverage are marked unreachable at start; devices never identified are shown as red dots.
newRun.staggerHint: Off: every reader starts its first frame at t = 0. On: readers start in groups, each group a fixed interval after the previous one. The grouping is a strategy and is stored with the run.

controller.title: Frame-size controller
controller.hint: How each reader chooses K and p* every round.
controller.autoFixed: Adaptive K is off → fixed K

desc.auto: Same behaviour as before this option existed: the Adaptive K switch decides between DFSA and fixed K.
desc.fixed: Every round uses the K and p* entered above.
desc.dfsa: Dynamic framed slotted ALOHA: K = 2N̂ from the backlog estimate of the previous frame.
desc.policy: A trained PPO policy from the registry chooses K and p* from each reader’s local observation. Each reader keeps its own recurrent state.

controller.noPolicies: No policy in the registry yet — train one and promote it (Training page).
controller.deterministicHint: Use the mean action instead of sampling from the policy distribution (reproducible runs).

resource.title: Multi-reader resources
resource.hint: How readers share time and frequency and whether they interfere.

desc.independent: Readers never interfere — the original thesis model and the golden regression.
desc.shared: Every reader uses all F subbands at the same time; overlapping coverage loses R2D/D2R messages.
desc.fdma: The conflict graph is coloured; each colour gets a disjoint group of the F subbands (fewer Msg1 subbands per reader).
desc.tdma: Each colour gets its own time slot in a repeating window; readers wait for their slot (serial within a conflict).
desc.hybrid: Colours are split into frequency groups first, then into time slots inside each group.
desc.lbt: A reader senses the channel before a frame and backs off while a conflicting reader transmits; ETSI dwell rule (max on-time, then a pause).

resource.singleReader: Only one reader is active: coordination has no effect.
resource.fFreqHint: Number of Msg1 frequency subbands (TR 38.769: F). K = L_s × F_r slots per frame.
resource.tdmaWindowHint: Length of one colour’s window in the TDMA superframe (colours × window). Default 0.5 s.
resource.freqGroupsHint: Hybrid: number of disjoint subband groups the colours are spread over; colours sharing a group take turns in time. Default 2.
resource.lbtBackoffHint: Wait after sensing a busy channel.
resource.lbtDwellHint: ETSI EN 302 208 style dwell: after the max on-time the reader must be silent for the pause (default 4 s / 0.1 s).
resource.linkBudgetHint: Two readers conflict if either one’s carrier reaches devices of the other above the SIR limit. Off: a plain distance threshold.
resource.nColorsHint: Empty = greedy colouring decides (minimum it finds).
resource.interferenceHint: Drop messages whose SIR/SINR is below the limits while overlapping readers transmit.
resource.crossMsg1Hint: Msg1 from devices of different readers on the same subband and slot collide.
resource.cwSuppressionHint: How much of another reader’s carrier the receiver cancels (TR 38.769 assumes self-interference cancellation).

termination.title: Reader termination
termination.hint: When a reader decides its population is done — without knowing the ground truth.

desc.oracle: The reader stops when no reachable device is left (simulator knowledge, the old behaviour).
desc.quiet_rounds: Stop after n consecutive frames with no new identification.
desc.id_rate: Stop when the identification rate over a window falls below an absolute or relative threshold.
desc.energy_bound: Stop once every device type has had the worst-case charging time (t_wc) since the last identification, so no sleeping device can still wake up.
desc.combined: Combine several rules with AND (all must fire) or OR (first one wins).

termination.rRelHint: Fraction of the peak rate seen so far.
termination.energySourceHint: Edge: the coverage-edge harvest (conservative). Actual: the reader’s own best-case device.
termination.edgeCapHint: Farthest distance used for the worst case. Device 2b is heard up to ~137 m but cannot harvest beyond ~62 m (ξ = 0 below −41 dBm), so without a cap t_wc is infinite and the rule never fires. 41.4 m = Device 2a coverage, the farthest backscatter device. Untick to use each type's own coverage radius.
termination.maxWaitHint: Upper bound on the wait after the last ID: the reader stops after min(t_wc × (1 + margin), this). Untick for no bound.

charts.termination: Termination rules: extra time vs missed devices

analysis.tNote: Tx = simulated time until x % of all devices in the scene are identified.

retention.hint: G = (T_serial − T_run) / (T_serial − T_ideal) on T99 of the reachable devices. 1 keeps the whole ideal multi-reader gain (independent readers), 0 is no better than serving conflicting readers one after another (TDMA).
retention.needTwo: Select at least two runs (ideal and serial references plus the runs to compare).
retention.unreached: A reference run never reached 99 % of its reachable devices — G is undefined.
retention.degenerate: The serial reference is less than 5 % slower than the ideal one, so readers barely conflict here and G is undefined or blows up. Pick references that differ, or a denser scene.

termination.hint: Each rule is replayed on the recorded frame history of one finished oracle run: how long after the last identification the readers would keep paging (extra time) against how many reachable devices they would leave behind. Bold rows are on the Pareto front.
termination.needFinished: Select at least one finished run.
termination.summary: {{reachable}} reachable · T99 {{t99}} s · last ID {{tLast}} s
termination.notOracle: This run already used a non-oracle rule; the replay only sees frames up to its own stop, so rules that would stop later are cut off.
termination.multiApprox: Several readers: each is replayed on its own frame history. A device its reader would only have found after stopping counts as missed, although in a live run a neighbouring reader might still have found it, so missed devices are an upper bound (see the design doc).
termination.zoomed: The axis is zoomed to the cluster. Rules that keep paging much longer (up to {{max}} s) are the triangles on the right edge.

interference.hint: Messages lost to other readers per run, the time readers waited for their TDMA slot / LBT backoff, and a per-frame timeline of the selected run.
interference.timelineHint: One row per reader; a marker is a frame, its size the number of lost messages.

devices.hint: Distributions over all devices of a finished run (and per device type in the table).

timeline.noEvents: No events for this device in the selected run.

charts.timeBin: Simulated time (s, all readers per bin)

ident.lead: Devices identified so far versus simulated time.
ident.body: X axis is simulated time, Y axis is how many devices some reader has successfully inventoried by then (count or percent). With one reader selected, only devices inside its coverage count. The earlier the curve reaches the top, the faster the inventory. T50 / T90 / T99 are read off this curve. The vertical line is the current live or replay time.

controller.lead: Per round: frame size K, access probability p*, and backlog estimate n̂.
controller.body: Top: K is the number of M1 slots the reader opens in this round (frame length), p* is the probability a device takes part; both are adjusted by the estimator from the previous round. Bottom: n̂ is how many devices the estimator believes are still unidentified, 'true backlog' is the real number, 'joiners' is how many actually took part. n̂ close to the true backlog means the estimator is accurate. With all readers selected only K and the true backlog are drawn, one line per reader.

outcome.lead: How each M1 slot ended, and the share of useful slots.
outcome.body: Each bar is one round (a time bin when all readers are shown), stacked by outcome: success = exactly one device answered, collision = several answered at once and drowned each other, empty = nobody answered. Resource efficiency = success / all slots, on the right axis in percent. Pure slotted ALOHA tops out around 36.8%.

timing.lead: How long each stage of a round took, in milliseconds.
timing.body: A round is paging (reader broadcasts the page) → M1 (devices answer in one of K random slots) → EBI (the reader broadcasts a K-bit map of which M1 slots it decoded) → M2 (reader acknowledges each winner) → M3 (device confirms). The stacked height is the whole round. Larger K makes M1 longer; more successes make M2 / M3 longer. With all readers selected the bars are averages per round within each time bin.

energy.lead: Stored energy of the devices now, and protocol energy spent over time.
energy.body: Left: histogram of the energy (µJ) each in-scope device has in its capacitor at the current time; devices on the far left are about to switch off. Right: cumulative energy each device type has spent sending and receiving protocol messages. A device that runs out mid-round is forced off to recharge and competes again later; those events are counted as depletions in Metrics.

round.lead: Slot-by-slot view of one M1 frame.
round.body: Each cell is one M1 slot: idle, single (one device, decoded), captured (several devices, the strongest was decoded), collision, or missed. The numbers above: candidates = awake devices allowed to take part; joiners = those that actually did, after p*; budget = how many winners M2 can acknowledge this round; budget dropped = winners not acknowledged for lack of budget, who retry next round; identified = devices finished in this round; true backlog = devices in this reader's coverage still unidentified. Use the slider to pick a round or follow the latest one.

metrics.lead: Summary numbers and breakdown tables for this run.
metrics.body: Cards: identified / unidentified / resource efficiency / rounds / depletions / unreachable. Per type: count, identified, T50, T99 and energy per device type. Depletions by stage: in which stage devices ran out of energy. Time overhead: total time and share per stage. Per reader: rounds, identified and efficiency for each reader.

pin.lead: Distribution of the strongest power each device receives from any reader.
pin.body: X axis is received power (dBm), Y axis is the fraction of devices receiving at most that power. A curve further right means devices are closer to a reader and harvest faster. One line per device type; compare with Figure 4 of the paper.

coord.lead: How the readers shared the spectrum and what they lost to each other.
coord.body: KPIs: coordination mode, number of colours, frames hit by interference, readers stopped. Bars: messages lost to interference over time per stage (R2D paging, Msg1, Msg2, Msg3). Table: per-reader colour, subbands, time slot, conflict neighbours, rounds, losses, deferred time (TDMA wait / LBT backoff), stop reason and t_wc.

terms.identified: Devices a reader has successfully inventoried.
terms.dropped: Devices still unidentified when the run ended: outside every reader’s coverage, time limit reached, or no progress (shown as red dots).
terms.unreachable: Devices outside every reader's coverage; they can never be inventoried.
terms.no_progress: The run ended by itself after the configured stall time (default 300 s simulated) without a single new identification.
terms.depletions: Times a device ran out of energy in the middle of a round and had to recharge.
terms.rounds: Rounds executed so far, all readers together.
terms.t50: T50 / T90 / T99: simulated time until 50 / 90 / 99 % of the devices were identified.
terms.K: Frame size: number of M1 slots in this round.
terms.pstar: p*: probability that an awake device takes part in this round.
terms.nHat: n̂: the estimator's guess of how many devices are still unidentified.
terms.backlogTrue: True backlog: actual number of unidentified devices in coverage.
terms.joiners: Devices that actually took part in the round after the p* draw.
terms.candidates: Awake devices that were allowed to take part.
terms.success: Slot with exactly one answering device.
terms.collision: Slot where several devices answered at once; none decoded.
terms.efficiency: Resource efficiency: successful slots divided by all slots.
terms.paging: Paging: the reader broadcasts the round parameters.
terms.m1: M1: devices answer in one of K random slots.
terms.ebi: EBI: the reader broadcasts a K-bit map of which M1 slots it decoded; its length grows with K.
terms.m2: M2: the reader acknowledges each decoded device.
terms.m3: M3: the acknowledged device replies and is identified.
terms.budget: Maximum number of winners M2 can acknowledge this round.
terms.budgetDropped: Winners not acknowledged because the budget ran out; they retry next round.
terms.energyNow: Energy stored in the device capacitor at the current time.
terms.energySpent: Cumulative energy spent on protocol messages.
terms.slotCodes: Cell colours: idle, single, captured, collision, missed.
terms.pin: Pin: strongest received power from any reader, in dBm.
terms.cdf: CDF: fraction of devices at or below the value on the X axis.
terms.conflictGraph: Conflict graph: an edge joins two readers whose carriers would break each other’s links (link budget or distance).
terms.colour: Colour: a graph colouring of the conflict graph; readers of one colour never conflict and share a resource.
terms.grant: Grant: the subbands and time slot a reader may use.
terms.r2dLost: R2D lost: devices that missed the paging because of another reader’s carrier.
terms.d2rLost: D2R lost: Msg1/Msg3 replies whose SINR at the reader was below the limit.
terms.deferred: Deferred: time a reader waited for its TDMA slot or LBT backoff/pause.
terms.stopReason: Stop reason: which termination rule ended the reader (or exhausted under the oracle).

training.title: Multi-reader RL training
training.subtitle: Experiments under backend/training: learning curves, generalization against DFSA and the policy registry used by runs.
training.noRuns: No run yet. Start one with the command above.
training.learningHint: One dot per training episode; the line is a rolling mean.
training.evalHint: Paired evaluation: the policy and DFSA see the same deployments (readers × device count × mix × offsets). Cell value T99 / DFSA, below 1 (green) means faster than DFSA.
training.promoteHint: Copies the checkpoint into rl/policies with a SHA-256 sidecar so New run can select it.

steps_.train: Train offline: cd Implements/backend && PYTHONPATH=. .venv/bin/python -m training.train --config <experiment> --scale small (smoke · small · medium · full, or a factor such as 0.5).

rl.title: How the RL policy decides
rl.subtitle: The training loop, top to bottom. Scroll for the action formulas, the reward, and the PPO update. A thesis run keeps your scene and uses the mean action.

map.cold: Cold start: K and estimator p*

sheet.inputLead: 41 numbers, each clipped to 0–1. A frame that has not happened is zeros.
sheet.frames: Last 4 frames, newest first. 8 numbers each.
sheet.join: devices that joined, divided by K
sheet.fr: granted subbands Fᵣ / all subbands F
sheet.quiet: time since its last new ID / 120 s
sheet.left: how many devices are still left
sheet.energy: how much energy each device has
sheet.outputLead: a₀ and a₁ are in −1…1. Each becomes a multiplier of the previous frame.
sheet.a: raw output. Deterministic mode, the default, uses the mean.
sheet.m: in [0.25, 10]. Scales the previous Msg1 length L. K = L × granted subbands Fᵣ.
sheet.q: in [0.1, 10]. Scales the previous p*, then clipped to 0.0001…1.

map.action: Turn the action into K and p*

legend.lead: This box sits to the left of the formulas. $e^{x}$ means e to the power x. $\exp(x)$ is the same writing. $e\approx 2.718$. $\ln$ is the log that undoes it: $\ln(e^{x})=x$.
legend.K: how many Msg1 resources this frame has
legend.p: probability that an awake device in range joins this frame
legend.L: Msg1 length. The resource count is this length times the granted subbands
legend.F: how many subbands exist in total
legend.Fr: how many of those subbands this reader was granted
legend.prev: the same quantity on this reader's previous frame
legend.Kcold: the cold-start size typed in New run
legend.Kmax: the largest K the system allows
legend.sigma: how far training may wander from $\mu$
legend.a: the two numbers actually used. $a_0$ sets $m$, $a_1$ sets $q$. Each is in $-1$ to $1$
legend.m: how many times larger or smaller the Msg1 length becomes
legend.q: how many times larger or smaller $p^*$ becomes
legend.ids: devices this reader identified for the first time in this frame
legend.coll: Msg1 resources where more than one device answered
legend.alpha: how much a collision counts against a new ID. $0.5$ means the same weight
legend.beta: how much this reader's own rate counts against the team rate. $0.5$ means half and half
legend.team: new IDs per second of every reader, since this reader's last decision
legend.rew: local and team mixed, then divided by 100. This is what PPO sees
legend.V: the critic's guess of the reward still to come
legend.r: the reward of this one decision
legend.delta: the surprise: reward, plus the discounted future, minus the guess
legend.boot: the future value that is allowed in. $0$ if the inventory really finished
legend.A: how much better this action was than the guess
legend.gamma: $0.99$. A reward one step later still counts as $99\%$
legend.lambda: $0.95$. Mixes the one-step surprise with a longer one
legend.d: $1$ if the episode ended on this step, otherwise $0$
legend.pi: the probability the actor gave this action
legend.rho: that probability now, divided by what it was when the action was taken
legend.eps: $0.2$. The update may not move that probability by more than $20\%$
legend.R: the training target for $V$. It equals $A+V$
legend.H: entropy. Higher means the actor is still willing to try other actions
legend.c: how hard the value error and the entropy pull. $c_V=0.5$, $c_H=0.005$
legend.g: 14 extra numbers only the MAPPO critic sees, and only while training
legend.n: how many decisions are stored before one update

full.sampleLead: Training starts here. Every episode draws a new warehouse. A thesis run does not: it keeps the scene you placed.
full.readers: Active readers, drawn uniformly from the config range. The randomized configs use $1$–$18$, on a random subset of the 18-reader lattice.
full.devices: Device count, drawn uniformly from the scale range. The published small runs use $100$–$400$.
full.offsets: Start offsets: none, uniform on $[0, 2\,\mathrm{s}]$, or two alternating groups.
full.resource: Resource mode: independent, FDMA, TDMA, or hybrid. The scheme is aperiodic.
full.mix: Subtype mix: equal thirds, or, with probability $1/2$, a single subtype.
full.coldLead: The first frame of each reader does not ask the network.
full.coldK: $K_{\mathrm{init}}=\max(8, K_{\mathrm{cold}})$. If $F_r<F$, then $K=\lceil K_{\mathrm{init}}/F\rceil\cdot F_r$. Otherwise $K=K_{\mathrm{init}}$.
full.actorLead: PS-PPO and MAPPO train a new MLP from scratch. They do not keep training the paper's LSTM.
full.net: $\mu(o)$ is an MLP $41\to 128\to 128$ with $\tanh$, then $2$ outputs. $\log\sigma$ is one learned vector, started at $-0.5$.
full.draw: Training draws $a\sim\mathcal{N}(\mu,\sigma)$ with $\sigma=e^{\log\sigma}$, then clips $a$ to $[-1,1]$.
full.mean: A thesis run sets $a=\mu$. Deterministic is the default in New run.
full.criticTitle: MAPPO critic input $g$, 14 numbers, training only
full.gStop: fraction of readers stopped or exhausted
full.gFrame: mean of each reader's latest 8 frame numbers
full.criticNote: PS-PPO's critic sees only the 41 numbers. A thesis run loads the actor and does not use the critic.
full.zero: Zero-shot is not this network and is not trained here. It copies the paper's LSTM onto every reader: 7 numbers from the latest frame, one memory per reader, and the same two multipliers.
full.actionLead: Training and a thesis run both use this map. $a_0,a_1\in[-1,1]$.
full.rewardLead: This is the number PPO learns from. A thesis run does not compute it.
full.team: $\mathrm{team}=$ (new IDs of every reader since this reader's previous decision) $\,/\,(t_{\mathrm{end}}-t_{\mathrm{prev}})$.
full.doneLead: The next decision is still the reader with the earliest clock, and it uses the same network.
full.stay: Readers still due: go back up. Same warehouse.
full.stop: Sample a new warehouse when every reachable device is identified, or the time cap, the stall timeout, or the frame cap is hit.
full.boot: All reachable devices identified is a real ending: the value target stops there. A time or frame cap is a cutoff, and the value of this state is reused.
full.count: Either way this decision counts. The update below runs after $n_{\mathrm{steps}}$ decisions in one environment, not at the end of every episode.
full.updateLead: Collected decisions are one interleaved stream per environment. Then training samples another warehouse until the step budget is spent.
full.gae: MAPPO, walking that stream backward: $\delta=r+\gamma\,\mathrm{boot}-V$, $\;A=\delta+\gamma\lambda(1-d)A_{\mathrm{next}}$. $\mathrm{boot}=0$ on a real ending, $V_{\mathrm{next}}$ while the episode continues, and $V$ of this state when it was cut off. $A$ is then standardized.
full.sb3: PS-PPO is this same clipped objective inside stable-baselines3, with a critic that sees only the 41 numbers. MAPPO's critic also sees $g$.
full.scale: The published runs are the small scale: $50\,000$ decisions, $4$ environments, $1024$ steps before each update, batch $256$, $5$ epochs. The full budget is $10^6$ decisions.
full.save: A thesis run loads the actor only.
full.evalLead: After the budget, the policy and DFSA play the same deployments and the same seeds. The number reported per cell is the T99 ratio.

who.title: Who acts
who.body: Readers do not take turns. The reader with the earliest clock runs the next frame, and that frame is one RL step. Every reader uses the same network.

decision.title: First frame
decision.body: The first frame of each reader skips the network. Later frames scale the previous K and p*.

cold.title: Cold start
cold.body: K is the cold-start value from New run, scaled to the subbands this reader was granted. p* comes from the backlog estimator.

input.title: Input
input.body: 41 numbers in 0–1. Eight from each of the last 4 frames, newest first: successes, collisions, empty resources, new IDs, joiners, frame size, p*, and duration. Nine more for this reader: how many readers, neighbours, colour, granted subbands, start delay, x, y, time since the last new ID, and frames already run. A missing frame is zeros. Devices still left, their stored energy, and who is awake are never observed.

network.title: Shared network
network.body: PS-PPO and MAPPO use one MLP: 41 → 128 → 128 (tanh) → 2. With Deterministic on, the output is the mean. Zero-shot copies the aperiodic paper’s LSTM onto every reader, with 7 numbers from the latest frame and its own memory. MAPPO’s critic sees the whole warehouse, but only while training.

output.title: Output
output.body: Two multipliers of the previous frame, not a raw K and a raw p*. m ∈ [0.25, 10] scales the Msg1 length L, then K = L × granted subbands Fᵣ. q ∈ [0.1, 10] scales p* into 0.0001…1. Example: L = 16, p* = 0.4, Fᵣ = 4, m = 2, q = 0.5 gives K = 128 and p* = 0.2.

frame.title: One frame
frame.body: The warehouse runs the chosen K and p*. Awake devices in range join with probability p* and pick one Msg1 resource. What happened becomes the next input. Training then draws a new warehouse; a thesis run keeps the scene you placed. The Seed in New run is this run’s energy phase and random access. The s0 in a policy id is the seed that trained the network.

reward.title: Training score
reward.body: local = ((1 − α) × new IDs of this reader − α × collisions) / frame duration. team = new IDs of every reader since this reader’s previous decision / elapsed time. reward = (β × local + (1 − β) × team) / 100. The published policies use α = 0.5 and β = 0.5. A thesis run does not compute this score.

flow.coldBody: K is the value from New run. p* comes from the backlog estimator. The network is not asked.
flow.netBody: One MLP for every reader. Deterministic mode, the default, uses the mean.
flow.netZero: Zero-shot is the exception: the paper’s LSTM, 7 numbers from the latest frame, one memory per reader. It still emits the same two multipliers.
flow.frameBody: Awake devices in range join with probability p* and each pick one of the K Msg1 resources. Successes, collisions and empty resources are the next observation.
flow.score: Training only. A thesis run does not compute this.
flow.inputFrames: Last 4 frames: S/K, C/K, E/K, new IDs/K, joiners/K, log₂(K), p*, duration.
flow.inputPlace: This reader: reader count, neighbours, colour, granted subbands, start delay, x, y, time since the last new ID, frames already run.
flow.inputHidden: Not included: devices still left, their energy, who is awake.
flow.outA: a₀, a₁, each in −1…1. Deterministic mode uses the mean.
flow.outM: m ∈ [0.25, 10] scales the previous Msg1 length. K = length × granted subbands.
flow.outQ: q ∈ [0.1, 10] scales the previous p*, clipped to 0.0001…1.
flow.train: Training draws a new warehouse each episode. A thesis run keeps the scene you placed. The Seed in New run is that run’s energy phase and random access. The s0 in a policy id is the seed that trained the network.

rl.select: Select a stage. The note underneath follows the selection.
rl.loop: The frame is then run. The reader with the next earliest clock is the next step, and it uses the same network.

who.title: The reader that is due
who.body: Readers do not take turns in a fixed order. The reader whose clock is earliest runs the next frame, and that frame is one decision.

input.title: What this reader already saw
input.body: The network receives 41 numbers, each clipped to 0–1. They are the last four frames of this reader, plus where the reader sits. A missing frame is zeros.

network.title: One shared network
network.body: PS-PPO and MAPPO use one MLP for every reader: 41 inputs, two hidden layers of 128 with tanh, then two outputs. With Deterministic on, which is the default in New run, the output is the mean. No extra noise is drawn.

output.title: How big, how often
output.body: The two outputs are multipliers of the previous frame, not a raw resource count and a raw probability. Resources then follow the subbands this reader was granted.

world.title: One inventory frame
world.body: Awake devices in range join with probability p* and each pick one of the K Msg1 resources. Successes, collisions and empty resources become the next input.

score.title: Used only while training
score.body: Training gives the decision a score. A thesis run does not. It only applies the K and p* from the output.

rl.inputLead: Only what a real reader can know. Counts are divided by K so a large frame and a small frame sit on the same scale.
rl.historyTitle: Last 4 frames, newest first — 8 numbers each

history.s: Msg1 resources that identified a device
history.ids: Devices identified for the first time in this frame
history.k: How large the frame was, on a log scale up to Kmax
history.t: How long the frame took, divided by 0.5 s

context.readers: How many readers are active, divided by 18
context.neighbors: How many neighbours it interferes with, divided by 17
context.color: Its coordination colour, divided by the number of colours
context.fr: Subbands it was granted, divided by all subbands F
context.offset: Its start delay, divided by 10 s
context.x: Horizontal position, divided by the warehouse width
context.y: Vertical position, divided by the warehouse height
context.quiet: Time since its last new ID, divided by 120 s
context.frames: Frames it has already run, divided by 2000

rl.hiddenLead: A reader cannot know these, so the network is not given them.

hidden.left: How many devices are still unidentified
hidden.energy: How much energy each device has stored
hidden.awake: Which devices are awake right now

rl.outputLead: Two numbers in −1…1. Each is turned into a multiplier of the previous frame.

output.a: The raw network output. Deterministic mode uses the mean of each.
output.m: Scales the previous Msg1 length L. The new length is clipped to at least 1 and at most what Kmax allows. K = L × the granted subbands F_r.
output.q: Scales the previous paging probability. The result is clipped to the range 0.0001…1.
output.first: The first frame of each reader skips the network. K is the cold-start value from New run, and p* comes from the backlog estimator. Later frames scale those.

rl.example: Previous frame: Msg1 length L = 16, p* = 0.4, and this reader was granted F_r = 4 subbands. The network emits multipliers m = 2 and q = 0.5. Next frame: L = 32, so K = 32 × 4 = 128 resources, and p* = 0.2.
rl.rewardLead: This number is how the network is trained. It is not sent back into the warehouse, and a live thesis run does not compute it.
rl.rewardLocal: local = ((1 − α) × new IDs of this reader − α × collisions) / frame duration
rl.rewardTeam: team = new IDs of every reader since this reader’s previous decision / elapsed time
rl.rewardNote: α is the weight on collisions. β is the weight on this reader against the whole warehouse. The published policies use α = 0.5 and β = 0.5. Dividing by 100 keeps the score near 1.
rl.algosLead: New run → controller “RL policy” loads one of these. The input and output above are the multi-reader MLP. The zero-shot policy is the exception.

ps.name: PS-PPO
ps.body: One MLP shared by every reader. Its value head, used only in training, sees the same 41 numbers. The reader count, neighbours and position inside the input let that one network behave differently per reader.

mappo.name: MAPPO
mappo.body: The same shared actor. During training a second network, the critic, also sees a 14-number picture of the whole warehouse: identified fraction, time, reader count, stopped readers, fraction awake, mean energy, and the average of the latest frame. That picture is not an input when the policy runs in a thesis simulation.

ippo.name: IPPO
ippo.body: One actor per reader slot, the reader’s index in that episode. Each critic sees only its own 41 numbers. There is no shared network and no warehouse-wide picture.

zero.name: Zero-shot
zero.body: The aperiodic paper’s LSTM, copied onto every reader with its own memory. Its input is 7 numbers from the latest frame only: new IDs of device types 1, 2a and 2b, empty resources, collisions, the Msg1 length, and p*. The output is still the same two multipliers.

rl.trainBody: Each training episode draws a new warehouse from the training seed: how many readers, which of the 18 lattice sites, start delays, resource mode, device count and device mix. A thesis run does not do that. It freezes the scene you placed. The Seed field of New run is the seed of that one warehouse’s energy phases and random access, not the seed that trained the network. The s0 in a policy id is the training seed.
